topics.claim: Hot dogs are sandwiches.
Cereal is a soup.
Pineapple belongs on pizza.
A straw has one hole.
Cats are better colleagues than dogs.
Time travel to the past is pointless even if possible.
Reading the last page of a book first is a legitimate way to read.
Every meeting should be a maximum of nine minutes.
Socks are footwear, so wearing only socks counts as being dressed.
Emojis are a real language.
The moon landing was easier than parallel parking.
Autocorrect has made humanity worse at thinking.
Voting should be mandatory.
Museums should return every artefact they did not make.
Anonymity online causes more harm than good.
Nostalgia is a form of lying to yourself.
Free will is a useful illusion, not a fact.
Tipping should be abolished.
Spoilers improve stories.
Homework should be illegal before age 14.
A remake can be better than the original.
Sports leagues should have no salary caps.
Silence should be a protected natural resource.
Handwriting should still be taught in schools.
There should be a legal right to be forgotten by the internet.
Small talk is the most important social skill.
Pluto should be reinstated as a planet.
Any book adaptation should be legally required to change the ending.
Cities should ban cars from their centres.
Boredom is necessary for creativity.
You should be able to sell your vote.
Art made by a machine can be great art.
Deadlines make work worse, not better.
Everyone should have to work one week a year in a job they hate.
Fiction teaches more truth than history.
Ghosting is sometimes the kindest option.
Sequels ruin more than they add.
The best coffee is the cheapest coffee.
Pockets should be standardised by law.
Public transport should be free.

judges.name: Judge Vex
judges.style: You score only on structure, evidence, and whether claims actually follow. Rhetorical flourish earns nothing. You are terse and a little disappointed.

judges.name: Judge Bloom
judges.style: You score on emotional truth, vividness, and whether an argument would move a real person in a real room. Dry technical points bore you.

judges.name: Judge Riot
judges.style: You score on nerve, surprise, and style. You reward a wild swing that lands and punish a safe, obvious point even if it's correct.
